answer: Each lift-bridge counterweight takes one agent: stake 80, fix a key-bound ivory mark to it, read it with a prism angle sight. The auditor re-derives the position from the public counterweight table, deck angle, span weight, temperature, and tower log; a wrong position, reused serial, or shared mark forfeits the stake. First filing 44, k-th 44+7(k-1), 1,000th 7,037; 1,000 fakes pay 3,540,500 plus 80,000 staked, each weight needs fresh calibration. A borrowed prism fails: its serial repeats, burning both stakes. An honest agent pays 44 once and recovers the stake after a clean audit.
